explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/83: Ahlswede–Khachatrian's complete intersection theorem says the maximum t-intersecting family of k-subsets of [m] is one of the families of k-sets with ≥ t+r elements from [t+2r]. The statement takes the weaker but correct form: for 2 ≤ t ≤ k ≤ m, every t-intersecting F is no larger than some such family, ∃ r. This omits the precise r condition, but that is harmless as a consequence of the theorem. Faithful.
